title: I Posted the Ramen-Broth Hours After They Camped My Numbered Stockpot

parts.text: I stepped into the broth bay at 4:03 a.m. and cook Kenji was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE POT. FOUR HOURS. TARE STAYS WITH THE SLOT. I was thirty-one, kitchen secretary, holding a clipboard that listed our numbered stockpot. Kenji shrugged. "Cooks are the broth." I photographed the board, the booking, and his leftover bones on my numbered stockpot. Then I asked for the broth log. At 4:11 the bay pinged why Kenji's name was on my bones. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The bay can see Kenji's leftover bones on my numbered stockpot.

social.video_title: They camped my numbered ramen stockpot — Part 1/2
social.description: Broth bay, leftover bones, a four-hour clock he posted. I logged the pot. Would you have asked for the broth log?

parts.text: Kenji called it extra extract until the bay asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the bone still. The stockpot went back to my numbered slot. Kenji ran a slot of his own and told the next cook atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: COOKS ARE NOT THE BROTH. I keep my tare in a labeled jug. Kenji brown-bags his extract. The bay finally looks like a slot, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Cooks are not the broth — Part 2/2
social.description: Broth log, numbered stockpot, and a second line on the board. Was extra extract ever my bones?
